title: 10.1 Small Group · Group 2
contentObjective: I can find applications of math outside of school — in professions like being a chef, in hobbies like gardening, and around my own house, explain why the method works, and use it on a problem I have not seen before.
languageObjective: I can justify my answer to a skeptic and connect it to a second strategy or representation.

noticeAndWonder.context: A busy restaurant kitchen. A chef reads a recipe card while cooks prep vegetables, and a whiteboard lists tonight's specials with prices.
noticeStarters: I notice the chef is looking at ___ .
wonderStarters: I wonder how the chef decides ___ .
I wonder what math is hiding in ___ .

turnAndTalk.question: The chef plans a planter that is 4 feet long and 2 feet wide, filled 1 foot deep with soil. What two different things does the chef calculate about that planter, and why are they different?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Area of the planter is 4 × 2 = 8 square feet (how many plants fit); volume is 4 × 2 × 1 = 8 cubic feet (how much soil to buy).

stems.en: The chef calculates ___ to find how many plants fit and ___ to find how much soil to buy.
stems.es: El chef calcula ___ para saber cuántas plantas caben y ___ para saber cuánta tierra comprar.

stems.en: Area and volume are different because ___.
stems.es: El área y el volumen son diferentes porque ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: If the same planter needed soil 2 feet deep instead of 1 foot, would the area change, the volume change, or both? Justify your answer.
extendStems: The area would ___ because ___, but the volume would ___ because ___.
Doubling the depth changes ___ from 8 to ___ cubic feet.

turnAndTalk.question: When you sorted the chef's tasks from the gardener's tasks, what made a card belong with 'calculating the volume of the planter' instead of 'calculating the area of the planter'?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Area (8 square feet) tells you how many plants fit; volume (8 cubic feet) tells you how much soil to buy.

stems.en: This card belongs with volume because it is about ___.
stems.es: Esta tarjeta va con volumen porque se trata de ___.

stems.en: This card belongs with area because it is about ___.
stems.es: Esta tarjeta va con área porque se trata de ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: A chef's inventory task and a gardener's soil task both involve counting or measuring amounts. Are they the same kind of math? Defend your answer.
extendStems: They are/are not the same kind of math because ___.
Inventory is about ___, while soil volume is about ___.

turnAndTalk.question: Turning off the water while brushing saves 4 gallons per brushing, twice a day, for 365 days — a total of 2,920 gallons a year. How is this the same kind of math as the chef ordering ingredients?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Both use multiplication to project a total amount from a smaller repeated quantity: 4 gallons × 2 brushings × 365 days = 2,920 gallons.

stems.en: This is like the chef's math because both ___ a small amount by ___ to project a total.
stems.es: Esto es como las matemáticas del chef porque ambos ___ una cantidad pequeña por ___ para proyectar un total.

stems.en: The water savings for one year is ___ gallons.
stems.es: El ahorro de agua para un año es de ___ galones.

turnAndTalk.extend: A household of 3 people each saves 2,920 gallons a year. Generalize a rule for finding the savings for any number of people, and use it to find the savings for 7 people.
extendStems: My rule is to multiply ___ by ___, so for 7 people the household saves ___ gallons.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice, when a problem gave you a rate — like gallons saved per day — what strategy helped you scale it up to a year?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A rate like 8 gallons a day scales up by multiplying by the number of days: 8 × 365 = 2,920.

stems.en: I found the total by ___ the daily amount by ___.
stems.es: Encontré el total al ___ la cantidad diaria por ___.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who added 8 + 365 instead of multiplying? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

vocabulary.definition: A job someone is trained to do, like chef, nurse, or carpenter.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un trabajo para el que alguien se ha preparado, como chef, enfermero o carpintero.
vocabulary.example: Chefs are found in restaurant kitchens overseeing food preparation.

vocabulary.definition: The supply of items a business keeps on hand, tracked by counting.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Las existencias que un negocio tiene disponibles, controladas contándolas.
vocabulary.example: A chef manages inventory so the kitchen never runs out of ingredients.

vocabulary.definition: The measured amount of food served to one person.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad medida de comida que se sirve a una persona.
vocabulary.example: Chefs decide on the portion size of each item on the menu.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of flat space a surface covers, measured in square units.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad de espacio plano que cubre una superficie, medida en unidades cuadradas.
vocabulary.example: Gardeners calculate the area of the planter to decide how many plants fit.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of space something fills, measured in cubic units.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad de espacio que algo ocupa, medida en unidades cúbicas.
vocabulary.example: Gardeners calculate the volume of the planter to know how much soil to buy.

launch.narrative: This is your challenge small group for Lesson 10.1. You can already get the answer — so in here the answer is the starting point. We ask when the method holds, when it breaks, and how you would convince someone who disagrees.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — Math is an integral part of nearly every profession
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: People use math every day in their professions and their hobbies — and it is a good tool for solving problems around your house, too — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me find the math in a chef's day
lines: When chefs plan menus, they determine the number of items on the menu and calculate the price point for each item.
They decide on the portion size of each item and project how much food is needed for each day.
They calculate how much of each ingredient to order — that is counting, measuring, and multiplying, all before a single dish is cooked.

explore.label: Who is using this math? Sort each task.

cards.text: Calculate the price point for each item
Decide on the portion size of each item
Project how much food is needed for each day
Calculate how much of each ingredient to order
Calculate the volume of the planter to find the amount of soil needed
Calculate the area of the planter to decide how many plants to plant
Measure how deep to plant each seed

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Both columns are full of math — that is the point. A profession and a hobby, and neither one can run without calculating, measuring, and projecting. After sorting, name one more task for each column. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

connect.scenario: Math is an integral part of nearly every profession, and many hobbies include applications of math. You just saw it in a restaurant kitchen and a vegetable garden.
connect.promptQuestion: How is math used in another profession or hobby that matters to you?
connect.prompt: Think of a profession or hobby you care about. To do it well, that person might ___ amounts or prices, ___ distances or portions precisely, and ___ ahead so the work gets done on schedule.

check.stem: A chef is deciding how many portions of a new dish to prepare tonight, based on how many customers are expected. Which math task is this?
choices: Projecting how much food is needed for the day
Setting the price of the dish
Naming the dish on the menu
check.explanation: Deciding how many portions to prepare based on expected customers is projecting food needs — a quantity task. Setting the price is a separate math task (not quantity). Decorating and naming a dish are not math tasks at all.

check.stem: A gardener knows the size of their planter box and wants to know how much soil to buy to fill it. What should the gardener calculate?
choices: The number of leaves per plant
check.explanation: Volume measures 3D capacity, which tells you how much soil fills the box. Area (a 2D measure of the top surface) tells you how many plants fit, not how much soil is needed, and perimeter only measures the boundary length.

check.stem: Leaving the water running while brushing wastes an average of 4 gallons compared to turning the water on only to rinse. If one person brushes twice a day for a year (365 days), how many gallons would they save by turning the water off?
check.explanation: 4 gallons × 2 brushings per day × 365 days = 2,920 gallons. 1,460 comes from forgetting to count both daily brushings, 730 comes from using too small a savings amount per brushing, and 5,840 comes from doubling the whole product instead of just the daily brushings.

connect.modelAnswer: A basketball coach uses math constantly. They calculate shooting percentages to decide who takes the last shot, and they plan practice time by dividing 90 minutes among drills. They even measure and compare stats from game to game to see who is improving.

onLevel.stem: One person saves 8 gallons of water a day by turning the water on only to rinse. How much water does that person save in a year (365 days)?
onLevel.explanation: 8 gallons a day × 365 days = 2,920 gallons in a year.
choiceFeedback: 373 comes from adding 8 + 365 instead of multiplying.
1,460 multiplies 365 by 4 — the savings from one brushing — instead of the full 8 gallons a day.
365 is just the number of days; it forgets to multiply by the gallons saved each day.
hints: This is a two-part question: which bin holds more AND by how many cubic inches. You need both volumes first.
Find each volume with V = l × w × h, then subtract the smaller total from the larger to get the difference.
Start with Bin A: 8 × 6 = 48, then × 5. Next do Bin B: 9 × 4 = 36, then × 7. Compare the totals.
onLevel.stemEs: Dos cajas de almacenamiento: la Caja A mide 8 × 6 × 5 pulgadas. La Caja B mide 9 × 4 × 7 pulgadas. ¿Cuál guarda más y por cuánto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Caja A: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Caja B: 9 × 4 × 7 = 252 in³. La Caja B guarda 12 in³ más.
hintsEs: Esta pregunta tiene dos partes: cuál caja guarda más Y por cuántas pulgadas cúbicas. Necesitas ambos volúmenes primero.
Halla cada volumen con V = l × a × h y luego resta el total menor del mayor para obtener la diferencia.
Empieza con la Caja A: 8 × 6 = 48 y luego × 5. Después la Caja B: 9 × 4 = 36 y luego × 7. Compara los totales.

onLevel.title: Added the Last Edge

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: A capsule is 6 long, 5 wide, and 3 tall

onLevel.correctWork: The student multiplied the first two edges correctly (6 × 5 = 30) but then added the height instead of multiplying it. Every edge must be multiplied: V = 6 × 5 × 3 = 90 cubic units.
hints: Look at the Calculate step. Was the height added or multiplied?
Multiply all three edges: 6 × 5 × 3 = 90 cubic units, not 6 × 5 + 3 = 33.
onLevel.explanation: The Calculate step starts fine with 6 × 5 = 30, but then the student writes + 3 instead of × 3, landing on 33. Volume multiplies every edge, so the correct work is V = 6 × 5 × 3 = 90 cubic units.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso Calcular empieza bien con 6 × 5 = 30, pero luego el estudiante escribe + 3 en lugar de × 3 y llega a 33. El volumen multiplica todas las aristas, así que el trabajo correcto es V = 6 × 5 × 3 = 90 unidades cúbicas.

You know the savings per day.
How many days are in a year?

practice.stem: If each person in a house saves 2,920 gallons a year, how much does a household of 3 people save in a year?
practice.explanation: 2,920 gallons per person × 3 people = 8,760 gallons a year.
choiceFeedback: 2,923 comes from adding 2,920 + 3 instead of multiplying.
973 (about 2,920 ÷ 3) divides instead of multiplying — more people save MORE water, not less.
5,840 multiplies by 2 people instead of 3.
hints: The prism's edges are 8 cm, 5 cm, and 4 cm. Volume means multiplying those edges, not adding them.
Apply V = l × w × h with all three numbers — leaving one out gives an area, not a volume.
Multiply 8 × 5 = 40 first, then multiply that result by the height, 4 cm.
practice.stemEs: Un prisma rectangular tiene largo 8 cm, ancho 5 cm y altura 4 cm. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
hintsEs: Las aristas del prisma son 8 cm, 5 cm y 4 cm. El volumen significa multiplicar esas aristas, no sumarlas.
Aplica V = l × a × h con los tres números: dejar uno fuera da un área, no un volumen.
Multiplica 8 × 5 = 40 primero y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 4 cm.
The prism's edges are 8 cm, 5 cm, and 4 cm. Volume means multiplying those edges, not adding them.
Apply V = l × w × h with all three numbers — leaving one out gives an area, not a volume.
Multiply 8 × 5 = 40 first, then multiply that result by the height, 4 cm.
practice.stemEs: Un prisma rectangular tiene largo 8 cm, ancho 5 cm y altura 4 cm. ¿Cuál es su volumen?
practice.explanationEs: Each person saves the same amount.

stem: A household of 5 saves 2,920 gallons per person per year. A household of 4 does the same. How much MORE does the household of 5 save than the household of 4?
explanation: 5 people save 5 × 2,920 = 14,600 gallons and 4 people save 4 × 2,920 = 11,680 gallons. The difference is 14,600 − 11,680 = 2,920 gallons — exactly one more person's savings.
choiceFeedback: 14,600 is the TOTAL for the household of 5, not the difference between the two households.
11,680 is the TOTAL for the household of 4, not the difference between the two households.
1 is just the difference in the number of people — each of those people saves 2,920 gallons.
hints: How many more people does the bigger household have?
One more person means one more person's yearly savings.
Each person saves 2,920 gallons a year.

stem: Choose another person who works in a restaurant — not the chef — and describe the math they would use.
modelAnswer: A server uses math all shift. They add up each table's bill, calculate the change for customers paying cash, and figure out their tips as a percent of each check. At the end of the night they total their tips to see what they earned.
sentenceStems: A ___ in a restaurant uses math when ___ .

extending.stem: A gardener's planter has an area of 8 square feet, and each plant needs 2 square feet of space to grow. How many plants fit in the planter?
extending.explanation: 8 square feet ÷ 2 square feet per plant = 4 plants.
choiceFeedback: 16 multiplies 8 × 2 instead of dividing — that would need a much bigger planter.
10 comes from adding 8 + 2 instead of dividing.
6 comes from subtracting 8 − 2 instead of dividing.
hints: You are splitting the area into equal shares of space.
How many groups of 2 square feet fit inside 8 square feet?
Divide 8 by 2.

extending.prompt: A box needs to hold exactly 60 cubic inches. Give three different sets of whole-number dimensions that work. Which set would make the box closest to a cube shape? Why might that matter?
extending.sentenceFrame: Option 1: ___ × ___ × ___. Option 2: ___ × ___ × ___. Option 3: ___ × ___ × ___. The ___ option is closest to a cube because ___. This matters because ___.
extending.hint: Find three different factor combinations of the target volume.
hints: You need three DIFFERENT whole-number triples that multiply to exactly 60, like l × w × h = 60.
Start with a factor pair of 60 (like 6 × 10), then split one factor into two numbers to make a triple.
Try 60 = 6 × 10, then break the 10 into 2 × 5 for one triple. Then hunt for triples whose numbers are closer to equal.
extending.explanation: Any three whole numbers whose product is 60 work, such as 1 × 6 × 10, 2 × 5 × 6, and 3 × 4 × 5. Of those, 3 × 4 × 5 is closest to a cube because its edges are nearest to equal, and a cube-like box uses less material for its surface while holding the same 60 cubic inches.
extending.explanationEs: Sirve cualquier trío de números enteros cuyo producto sea 60, como 1 × 6 × 10, 2 × 5 × 6 y 3 × 4 × 5. De esos, 3 × 4 × 5 es el más parecido a un cubo porque sus aristas son las más cercanas entre sí, y una caja parecida a un cubo usa menos material en su superficie aunque guarde las mismas 60 pulgadas cúbicas.
extending.promptEs: Una caja debe contener exactamente 60 pulgadas cúbicas. Da tres conjuntos distintos de dimensiones con números enteros que funcionen. ¿Cuál conjunto haría la caja más parecida a un cubo? ¿Por qué podría importar eso?
hintsEs: Necesitas tres tríos DIFERENTES de números enteros que multiplicados den exactamente 60, o sea l × a × h = 60.
Empieza con una pareja de factores de 60 (como 6 × 10) y luego parte un factor en dos números para formar un trío.
Prueba 60 = 6 × 10 y luego parte el 10 en 2 × 5 para un trío. Después busca tríos cuyos números sean más parecidos entre sí.

extending.stem: A shipping crate is 12 ft long, 3 ft wide, and 2 ft tall. How many 1-foot cubes exactly fill it?
extending.explanation: The number of unit cubes equals the volume: 12 × 3 × 2 = 72 cubes.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The number of unit cubes equals the volume: 12 × 3 × 2 = ___ cubes.
Add dimensions or divide incorrectly? The volume (12 × 3 × 2) equals unit cubes.
Verify: 12 × 3 = 36, then 36 × 2 = ? cubes.
hints: Each 1-foot cube takes up exactly 1 ft³, so the number of cubes equals the crate's volume in cubic feet.
Find the crate's volume with V = l × w × h — that total IS the number of unit cubes that fit.
Start with one layer: 12 × 3 = 36 cubes. Then multiply by the height, 2 ft, for the number of layers.
extending.stemEs: Una caja de envío mide 12 ft de largo, 3 ft de ancho y 2 ft de alto. ¿Cuántos cubos de 1 pie la llenan exactamente?
extending.explanationEs: La cantidad de cubos unitarios es igual al volumen: 12 × 3 × 2 = 72 cubos.
hintsEs: Cada cubo de 1 pie ocupa exactamente 1 pie³, así que el número de cubos es igual al volumen del cajón en pies cúbicos.
Halla el volumen del cajón con V = l × a × h: ese total ES el número de cubos unitarios que caben.
Empieza con una capa: 12 × 3 = 36 cubos. Luego multiplica por la altura, 2 pies, para el número de capas.

extending.stem: Two prisms have the same volume of 48 cm³. Prism A is 4 × 4 × 3. Prism B is 8 × 3 × h. What is h?
extending.explanation: Prism A volume = 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cm³. For Prism B, h = 48 ÷ (8 × 3) = 48 ÷ 24 = 2 cm.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Prism A volume = 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cm³.
Use the formula: h = Volume ÷ (length × width).
Verify: 8 × 3 × h = 48. What value of h works?
hints: Both prisms hold 48 cm³. Prism B gives you two edges (8 and 3) and hides the height h.
Use h = Volume ÷ (length × width): divide 48 by the product of Prism B's two known edges.
Multiply 8 × 3 = 24 first. Then find what number times 24 equals 48.
extending.stemEs: Dos prismas tienen el mismo volumen de 48 cm³. El Prisma A mide 4 × 4 × 3. El Prisma B mide 8 × 3 × h. ¿Cuánto vale h?
extending.explanationEs: Volumen del Prisma A = 4 × 4 × 3 = 48 cm³. Para el Prisma B, h = 48 ÷ (8 × 3) = 48 ÷ 24 = 2 cm.

extending.stem: A time capsule box is 5 units long, 3 units wide, and 2 units tall. How many unit cubes fill it?
extending.explanation: V = length × width × height = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cubic units.
choiceFeedback: Add the three dimensions, not multiply them. How many cubes fill the entire box?
Did you include all three dimensions? You need length × width × height.
Try multiplying the three dimensions in the order: length × width × height.
extending.stemEs: Una caja de cápsula del tiempo mide 5 unidades de largo, 3 unidades de ancho y 2 unidades de alto. ¿Cuántos cubos unitarios la llenan?
extending.explanationEs: V = largo × ancho × altura = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 unidades cúbicas.
hints: Volume counts how many unit cubes fit inside a solid, so the answer will be in cubic units.
Use V = length × width × height and put all three given measurements into that formula.
Start with the bottom layer: 5 × 3 = 15 cubes in one layer. Now use the height to finish.
hintsEs: El volumen cuenta cuántos cubos unitarios caben dentro de un cuerpo, así que la respuesta irá en unidades cúbicas.
Usa V = largo × ancho × altura y coloca las tres medidas dadas en esa fórmula.
Comienza con la capa de abajo: 5 × 3 = 15 cubos en una capa. Ahora usa la altura para terminar.

hintsEs.stem: What factors do you consider to determine the number of plants you can put in a planter garden? Is the TYPE of plant a factor? Explain your thinking.
hintsEs.modelAnswer: I would consider the area of the planter and how much space each plant needs between it and its neighbors. The type of plant is definitely a factor, because a tomato plant needs much more space than a radish — so the same 8-square-foot planter could hold many radishes but only a few tomato plants.
sentenceStems: The type of plant matters because ___ .

hintsEs.stem: Which statement matches this lesson's big idea?
choices: Math is everywhere — in professions, hobbies, and problems around your house
Math is just a school subject with little relevance outside the classroom
Only professions like chef use math; hobbies do not
Math is only useful for people who work with money
hintsEs.explanation: The lesson's summary says it directly: some people think math is just a school subject, but math is everywhere — in professions, hobbies, and around the house.
choiceFeedback: That is exactly the belief the lesson set out to disprove.
The gardening half of the lesson showed a HOBBY full of area, volume, and measurement.
The chef, the gardener, and the water problem all used math about food, space, and water — not just money.
hints: Volume is the total number of unit cubes inside, no matter how they are grouped.
When cubes are stacked in identical layers, multiply the cubes in one layer by the number of layers.
One layer holds 6 cubes, so two layers hold 12. Keep going until you have accounted for all 4 layers.

Think about all three contexts in this lesson.
A profession, a hobby, and a bathroom sink.
What did they have in common?

hintsEs.stem: Each person saves 2,920 gallons a year. Which correctly compares households of 3, 4, 5, and 8 people?
choiceFeedback: 20,440 is 7 × 2,920 — the last household has 8 people, not 7.
Those add the household size to 2,920 instead of multiplying by it.
46,720 is 16 × 2,920 — that doubles the 8-person household instead of computing it.
hints: Each household total is people × 2,920.
Check the last value most carefully.

hintsEs.stem: Someone says, 'Math is just a school subject. I'll never use it after class.' Using the chef, the gardener, or the water problem, write what you would say back.
hintsEs.modelAnswer: I would say that a chef never stops using math — they calculate prices, portion sizes, and how much of each ingredient to order every single day. Even at home, math showed us that one person who turns off the tap while brushing saves 2,920 gallons a year. You do not escape math after class; you just stop noticing you are using it.

hintsEs.stem: A chef expects 120 customers tonight and projects that 1 out of every 4 will order the soup. Each serving of soup uses 2 cups of broth. How much broth should the chef prepare?
hintsEs.explanation: 120 ÷ 4 = 30 soup orders, and 30 orders × 2 cups each = 60 cups of broth.
choiceFeedback: 240 uses all 120 customers × 2 cups — but only 1 in 4 customers orders the soup.
30 is the number of soup ORDERS; it forgets to multiply by the 2 cups each serving needs.
15 divides the 30 orders by 2 instead of multiplying by 2.
hints: First find how many customers will order soup.
120 ÷ 4 = 30 orders.
Now, how many cups do 30 servings need?

hintsEs.stem: Pick a hobby — yours or anyone's — and list at least three specific math tasks hiding inside it, the way the lesson did for gardening.
hintsEs.modelAnswer: In skateboarding: you measure the height and length of a ramp to know if you can clear it, you count how many tries a trick takes and track whether that number is going down, and you estimate speed and distance before a gap so you know how hard to push. The board itself is measured in inches, and riders compare deck widths like 8.0 versus 8.25.

hintsEs.stem: A planter is 4 feet long and 2 feet wide. What is its area?
hintsEs.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma rectangular con l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in?
hintsEs.explanationEs: V = l × w × h = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs: Fíjate en las tres aristas: l = 7 pulg, a = 3 pulg, h = 4 pulg. El volumen pregunta cuánto espacio llena toda la caja.
Usa la fórmula del volumen V = l × a × h, y recuerda que el volumen se mide en unidades cúbicas (pulg³).
Empieza con 7 × 3 = 21 para la base y luego multiplica ese resultado por la altura, 4 pulgadas.
hintsEs.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el volumen de un prisma rectangular con l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in?
hintsEs.explanationEs: V = l × w × h = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 pulgadas cúbicas.
hintsEs.explanation: Area of a rectangle is length × width: 4 × 2 = 8 square feet.
choiceFeedback: 6 comes from adding 4 + 2 instead of multiplying.
12 comes from adding all four sides (4 + 2 + 4 + 2) — that is the perimeter, not the area.
2 comes from dividing 4 by 2 instead of multiplying.
hints: Area tells how much flat space the planter covers.
For a rectangle, multiply length by width.
Multiply 4 × 2.

choicesEs.commonMistake: Believing math only 'counts' when it happens in a classroom — and walking past the calculating, measuring, and projecting inside jobs, hobbies, and chores every day.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — Which statement best shows what this lesson means by 'math is everywhere'?
choices: People use math every day in their professions and hobbies, and it solves problems around the house too
Math only appears in jobs that involve money
Math is a school subject with little relevance to life outside the classroom
Only trained professionals like chefs are able to use math
exitTicket.explanation: The summary makes the claim in three parts: professions use math, hobbies use math, and it is a good tool for problems around your house.
hints: Look back at the Summarize slide.
It names professions, hobbies, AND your house.
Which option keeps all three?

questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 1), (5, 1), (5, 4), (1, 4). What is its perimeter?
What is the distance between (-4, 3) and (2, 3)?
questions.explanation: Both points have y = 3, so this is a horizontal distance. |2 - (-4)| = |2 + 4| = 6 units.

questions.stem: What is the distance between (5, -2) and (5, 4)?
questions.explanation: Both points have x = 5, so this is a vertical distance. |4 - (-2)| = |4 + 2| = 6 units.
